title: The ancient world, 4000–1000 BCE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: Uruk and the first cities of Mesopotamia
events.summary: Uruk grows into one of the first large cities. Its period gives its name to the age.

events.title: Writing begins in Mesopotamia
events.summary: Scribes in southern Mesopotamia turn accounting marks into cuneiform. It is the earliest known writing system.

source.quote: developed from pictographic proto-writing in the late 4th millennium BC

events.title: Ur-Nammu builds the ziggurat of Ur
events.summary: King Ur-Nammu raises a stepped temple tower for the moon god at Ur.

source.quote: built during the Early Bronze Age (21st century BC) by King Ur-Nammu

events.image: File:Royal Akkadian Head from Nineveh (inv.nr. IM 11331).jpg
events.title: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire
events.summary: Sargon of Akkad unites the city-states of southern Mesopotamia. Many call it the first empire.

source.quote: an ancient kingdom established around 2300 BC

events.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh takes written form
events.summary: Scribes join older Sumerian poems into one Akkadian epic. It is the oldest surviving narrative literature.

events.title: The Code of Hammurabi
events.summary: Hammurabi of Babylon has a code of laws carved on a tall stone stele.

source.quote: a Babylonian legal text composed c. 1753 BC

events.title: Egypt and the Hittites fight at Kadesh
events.summary: Ramesses II of Egypt meets the Hittite army of Muwatalli II on the Orontes River.

events.title: The Late Bronze Age collapse
events.summary: Kingdoms across the eastern Mediterranean fall or shrink. Cities such as Ugarit are destroyed.

source.quote: during the late 13th to early 12th century BC

events.title: Narmer unites Egypt
events.summary: Many scholars see Narmer as the first king of a unified Egypt. He founds the First Dynasty.

source.quote: whose reign began at the end of the 4th millennium BC

events.title: The Step Pyramid of Djoser
events.summary: Egypt builds its first pyramid as a tomb for King Djoser.

source.quote: built in the 27th century BC during the Third Dynasty

events.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza
events.summary: Workers build the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu over about 26 years. It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders.

source.quote: It was built c. 2600 BC over a period of about 26 years.

events.title: The Kingdom of Kerma rises in Nubia
events.summary: A Nubian kingdom grows at Kerma on the Nile. At its height it rivals Egypt.

quote: The culture developed from around 2500 BC
Around 1500 BC, it was absorbed into the New Kingdom of Egypt

events.title: The Hyksos rule northern Egypt
events.summary: Kings of foreign origin rule Lower and Middle Egypt from Avaris in the Nile Delta.

events.image: File:Kneeling figure, Nok culture, terracotta, Honolulu Museum of Art, 8348.1.JPG
events.title: The Nok culture appears in West Africa
events.summary: A farming culture in central Nigeria later makes the region's earliest known terracotta sculptures.

source.quote: Nok culture may have emerged in 1500 BCE

events.title: The Bantu expansion begins
events.summary: Bantu-speaking farmers begin a slow spread across central and southern Africa. It lasts for thousands of years.

events.title: Akhenaten moves Egypt's capital to Amarna
events.summary: Akhenaten builds a new capital and puts the sun disc Aten above the other gods.

events.title: Tutankhamun reigns
events.summary: The boy king restores Egypt's traditional gods after Akhenaten. He dies at about 19.

events.title: Newgrange passage tomb is built
events.summary: Farmers in Ireland build a great passage tomb above the River Boyne. It is older than the pyramids.

source.quote: built during the Neolithic Period, around 3100 BC

events.title: Ötzi the Iceman lives in the Alps
events.summary: A man dies high in the Alps, and the ice preserves his body. It is Europe's oldest known natural mummy.

events.title: Stonehenge is begun
events.summary: People dig the first ditch and bank on Salisbury Plain. The stones are set up in later centuries.

source.quote: Deposits containing human bone date from as early as 3000 BC

events.image: File:Bull leaping fresco, Knossos, 1600-1450 BC, AMH, 258363.jpg
events.title: The first palace rises at Knossos
events.summary: The Minoans of Crete build a palace at Knossos. It becomes their largest center.

source.quote: The first palace was built around 1900 BC

events.title: The eruption of Thera
events.summary: A huge volcanic eruption destroys Akrotiri on Thera. Its exact date is still debated.

events.title: Mycenae at its height
events.summary: The Mycenaean Greeks extend the great walls of their citadel at Mycenae.

source.quote: around 1250 BC or so, the Cyclopean wall was extended

events.title: The Sintashta culture in the southern Urals
events.summary: People of the southern Urals build fortified settlements. Many scholars link them to the earliest Indo-Iranian languages.

source.quote: dated to the period c. 2200–1900 BCE

events.title: The Indus Valley Civilisation at its height
events.summary: Planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro flourish along the Indus. The civilisation covers more land than Egypt and Mesopotamia combined.

source.quote: in its mature form from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE

events.title: The hymns of the Rigveda are composed
events.summary: Poets in the northwest of India compose Sanskrit hymns. They become the oldest of the four Vedas.

events.image: File:British Museum Chinese jade Neolithic period Liangzhu culture Cong 11022019 1433.jpg
events.title: The Liangzhu culture on the Yangtze delta
events.summary: A jade-working society builds a large center near modern Hangzhou. It may be one of East Asia's first states.

events.title: A large Jōmon village at Sannai-Maruyama
events.summary: Jōmon people in northern Japan settle a village with hundreds of pit houses.

events.title: The Erlitou culture
events.summary: A Bronze Age society grows in the Yellow River valley. Many archaeologists see it as China's first state.

source.quote: a narrower date range of 1750–1500 BC

events.image: File:Inscribed oracle bone, Shang Dynasty, Xiaotun, Anyang, Henan.jpg
events.title: The Shang dynasty rules the Yellow River valley
events.summary: Shang kings rule from capitals such as Yin. Their oracle bones hold the earliest known Chinese writing.

events.title: The Zhou defeat the Shang at Muye
events.summary: King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king. The Zhou dynasty begins.

events.title: Caral and the Norte Chico cities
events.summary: Communities on the coast of Peru build large plazas and mounds. It is the oldest known civilization in the Americas.

quote: a period of decline around 1800 BCE

events.image: File:Valdivia Female Figurine 2600-1500 BCE Brooklyn Museum.jpg
events.title: The Valdivia culture of coastal Ecuador
events.summary: Villagers on the Ecuador coast make some of the earliest pottery in the Americas.

events.image: File:Mound A at the Monumental Earthworks Poverty Point World Heritage Site.jpg
events.title: The earthworks of Poverty Point
events.summary: People in the lower Mississippi valley build great earthen ridges and mounds.

events.title: The oldest known Mesoamerican ballcourt
events.summary: Villagers on the Pacific coast of Chiapas build a court for the Mesoamerican ballgame.

events.title: The Olmec center at San Lorenzo
events.summary: The Olmec make San Lorenzo their main center. They carve colossal stone heads.

source.quote: the major center of Olmec culture from 1400 BCE to 900 BCE

events.title: Austronesian voyagers sail out of Taiwan
events.summary: Seafarers from Taiwan begin settling the islands of Southeast Asia. Their descendants later reach the Pacific and Madagascar.

events.image: File:Decorated piece of Lapita pottery from the Bourewa site in Fiji.jpg
events.title: Lapita settlers reach Island Melanesia
events.summary: Austronesian seafarers with stamped pottery settle Island Melanesia. They are ancestors of the Polynesians.
